comment: Hand-labeled seed questions: a developer's sentence, and the declarations that answer it. No query names an identifier the code uses, because the point is mapping words onto nodes. Label a declaration `<file>#<name>`, or `<file>#<Type>.<method>` when a method name is shared.

seeds.query: where does a comma-separated document become records?
what reads one line of key-value pairs?
where do accepted records end up?
which function announces the finished batch?
what makes sure a record carries the field it must?
where is the worst level in a batch worked out?
which entry point takes the comma-separated feed?
what part of the flow do both feeds share?
where is a named value read off a record?
which type holds a group of records together?
what counts how many records sit at each level?
where is the first row read as column names?
which function throws away the records that did not pass?
what turns a failure into a sentence a person reads?
where do the rows that could not be read get announced?
which function marks a record with where it came from?
what keeps count of the records that were thrown away?
where does the flow decide a record has enough columns?
